metadata.title: Logix / AION recurring unit cost assessment
metadata.price_basis: nominal dollars of each snapshot year; no conversion to current money
metadata.source_note: Baseline commit; source hashes identify the edited inputs used for this build.
metadata.estimate_status: engineering planning scenario; no supplier quotes; not audited manufacturing accounts

included: Purchased BOM and internal-chip recurring fabrication
Direct and test labor plus 35% employment burden
Process consumables, materials lost to yield and rework
Inbound/outbound logistics allowance to US distribution/customer
Explicitly bundled support delivery; service rows use their stated units
excluded: Land, factory construction and equipment purchases
Capital depreciation, equipment leases and financing
Original masks, tooling and fixture NRE
Software and firmware development, including maintenance-release development
Profit, income/sales tax and working-capital interest
scope.boundary: US production/distribution scenario. Purchased parts retain vendor margins/capital in their purchase price. Routine maintenance is included; Logix-owned capital cost is excluded. No fleet-wide total is calculated: rows include overlapping bundles and alternatives.

assumptions.offering_policy: Introduction on/before June 15 qualifies as offered, not proven shipment. No withdrawals are specified: earlier models/versions remain in the scenario. PRO is marked announced/shipping unconfirmed. Non-shipping RAM expansion targets excluded as factory configurations.
assumptions.scale: Planning scale: 10,000 hardware units per family/year, OEM electronics orders generally 10k–100k pieces; PRO 1,000/year, cartridges/printed editions 5,000 copies. Volumes are assumptions, not story facts. Steady recurring runs even at recently announced launches; ramp risk in high range.
assumptions.assembly_learning: 5 percentage points less assembly time each year relative to 1978 baseline; new/complex designs retain larger operation-hour budgets.
assumptions.logistics: Per-unit bulk US freight/handling allowance. No individually quoted route or international customs model.
assumptions.custom_fabrication: 75 mm NMOS wafer assumption, die area and yield per chip below. Advanced design/mask access does not eliminate recurring wafer processing or failures. No capital/NRE allocation.
assumptions.royalties: CP/M 10 USD/copy, CP/M networking 5 USD, Microsoft BASIC 20 USD; provisional contract allowances, not sourced contract terms. Owned software has no external royalty.
assumptions.service_units: Support is per customer-year; training is per learner at 8 learners and 6 teaching hours/day plus 1.5 prep hours/class/day. Unspecified course lengths are scenario assumptions. No repair-parts entitlement is assumed unless stated.
assumptions.uncertainty: Hardware/software ranges usually 0.70–1.60× central; PRO 0.65–1.75×; OEM silicon 0.50–2.50×; services 0.55–1.90×. Correlated scenario envelopes, not statistical intervals. Custom chip yield and 64K DRAM procurement dominate risk.
assumptions.double_counting: Nested BOMs count each component once. Final manuals/cartons/freight applied only at the top-level offer. Chip fabrication labor/energy is categorized inside the breakdown; extended BOM line costs include these internal conversion costs and must not be added to the total again.
assumptions.second_source: June 1979 cards use AION chips. SMC procurement is a separate conditional scenario from October 1979; June 1980/1981 comparisons do not assert a purchasing switch or a price reduction.
assumptions.joint_dri: DRI remains a separately owned licensor despite Adam’s minority stake. Existing provisional per-copy CP/M allowance remains; the $250,000 founder capital commitment is excluded from unit costs.

sources.title: BLS via FRED: manufacturing production-worker average hourly earnings
sources.used_for: June nominal wage anchors: 5.99, 6.54, 7.08, 7.85 USD/h. Benefits factor and skill multipliers are assumptions.

sources.title: EIA Annual Energy Review Table 8.10
sources.used_for: Annual US industrial electricity proxies: 2.8, 3.1, 3.7, 4.3 cents/kWh. Annual rates are retrospective proxies, not June-specific tariffs.

sources.title: BYTE November 1978 advertising
sources.used_for: Retail 4116 kit price sanity check only. OEM DRAM prices are scenario discounts; this later-1978 advertisement is not a June quote.
